dedupe_keys.name: subsea cables what is at stake enisa report on subsea cable resilience and protection july 2023

description: This ENISA report examines the resilience of the subsea cables that carry more than 97% of the world's internet traffic. It covers national regulatory regimes, international treaties and installation and repair permits, the subsea cable ecosystem and maps, and challenges for resilience, including ICPC statistics for cable faults and root causes: system failures, human error, natural phenomena and malicious actions, and technical causes such as power outages and shunt faults. The executive summary states that there were more than 378 cables worldwide in 2019 spanning more than 1.2 million kilometres, that about 150 to 200 accidental faults occur every year, mostly from fishing and shipping, that landing stations are weak points, and that scarce specialised repair ships mean a coordinated attack could have a major impact. It lists recommendations on authority mandates, monitoring, incident notification, landing station protection, route diversification and burial in shallow waters. Producer: ENISA, July 2023, prepared with input from interviews with cable industry and security experts. Coverage: global cable system with an EU policy focus. Access: free PDF; the front matter, contents and executive summary were read, the chapters were not read in full. Licence and cost: free; reproduction authorised with acknowledgement. Caveats: the fault statistics are quoted from other sources such as ICPC and CSIS. Simulation uses: the fault rates, causes and repair constraints give inputs for resilience and cascading-failure scenarios of international connectivity.
